subject: Archaeology
title: Rising Seas and Coastal Heritage
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Rising Seas and Coastal Heritage.

hook.text: Rising seas threaten thousands of coastal sites, from Pacific islands to Scotland.

buildup.text: Skara Brae in Orkney, a 5,000-year-old village, is eroding from violent winter storms.

discovery.text: Pacific islands lose burial grounds and sacred sites as atolls shrink and waves eat land.

twist.text: Many threatened sites have never been recorded. They may vanish before anyone knows.

climax.text: CITiZAN trains volunteers to photograph eroding coastal sites before the sea claims them.

punchline.text: The sea is rising. It does not check for heritage status.

quiz.question: What is happening to Skara Brae in Orkney?
options: Tourism damages structures faster than they can be repaired
Violent winter storms are eroding the 5,000-year-old site
Local development encroaches on the protected area

details.summary: Rising sea levels threaten thousands of coastal archaeological sites worldwide — from Pacific Island villages to Scottish brochs to Florida shell mounds. Erosion, saltwater intrusion, and storm surge are destroying evidence of millennia of human coastal settlement before it can be recorded.
details.whyItMatters: Humans have lived along coastlines for tens of thousands of years. Rising seas from climate change are erasing this record faster than archaeologists can document it, and the loss is irreversible.
takeaways: Rising seas threaten thousands of coastal heritage sites globally
Erosion and saltwater intrusion destroy archaeological deposits
Most threatened sites have never been formally recorded

faq.question: Which types of sites are most threatened by rising seas?
faq.answer: Low-lying coastal settlements, Pacific Island villages, Mediterranean harbor cities, and Arctic coastal sites on melting permafrost face the greatest threats. Shell middens, shipwrecks newly exposed by erosion, and entire landscapes of human occupation are disappearing.

faq.question: Can anything be done to save coastal heritage from rising seas?
faq.answer: Some sites can be protected with sea walls or managed retreat strategies, but most cannot be saved physically. The priority is rapid recording through drone survey, 3D scanning, and systematic excavation of the most significant threatened sites before they are lost.
